messages:
jess: heads up — bumped into a weird console bug where switching orgs briefly shows another org's projects in the sidebar. repro is pretty consistent for me.
ojess: steps: 1) sign in, 2) open /console/projects, 3) quick-switch org via topbar, 4) see ghost rows for ~1s then corrected.
owen: ugh. can you paste any console logs or network traces?
ojess: here's the fetch that looks suspicious: 
GET /api/internal/projects/prefetch?limit=20 
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer xxx
  X-Org-Id: 999
  X-Route: console-prefetch
Response 200 with body for org 123 (not 999) — so response payload mismatches request header.
opriya: that smells like a cache key normalization issue. prefetch layer might be dropping X-Org-Id when normalizing keys for the edge cache.
olee: could be the proxy rewrite logic. we recently landed the header-strip change for CDN health. @priya any chance you saw this in telemetry?
opriya: yes — noticed an uptick in "console.prefetch.mismatch" traces in last 24h, most from eu-west. traces show key = request.path + query but missing org header.
ojess: curious: quota/telemetry shows tokens billed to correct org though — so API gateway attribution still fine, just the prefetch cache return is wrong.
owen: wait so gateway attributes correct but cached response is cross-org. that implies cache store uses wrong key and doesn't vary on org. can we confirm the cache key code?
opriya: snippet from edge caching policy (rough):
cacheKey = path + sorted(query + headers.whitelisted)
whitelisted = ["Accept", "User-Agent"]
# X-Org-Id not whitelisted currently
olee: oh. that explains it. we excluded org header intentionally to increase cache hit rate, but side-effect is cross-org leakage for project list which is org-scoped. bad call.
ojess: timeline: this started after the cache whitelist change last week and correlates with a canary that raised prefetch hits.
infra-bot: alert: deploy 2026-03-14T12:34:00 canary to edge-proxy increased cache-hit ratio by 8% in eu-west.
deploy-bot: canary 2026-03-14T12:34:00 for edge-proxy rolled out to 10% hosts (id: dp-20260314-ep).
owen: short term: flip the whitelist to include X-Org-Id for /api/internal/projects/* and mark projects endpoint as Vary: X-Org-Id. longer term we need per-tenant cache isolation policy.
opriya: agree. also add telemetry counter for "cache.vary.missing_header" with endpoint and env.
olee: patch idea: add conditional keying: if path startsWith /api/internal/projects or /api/console then include X-Org-Id. generic endpoints can stay header-agnostic.
ojess: can we hotfix this in edge-proxy today? it's only a brief leak but it's still PII-ish if project names are private.
owen: i'm on it. i'll open a patch PR and a rollout plan: disable global header-strip, add X-Org-Id to whitelist for affected path, canary to 5% then 50% then 100%.
opriya: I'll add a QuickSight/Telemetry dashboard tile to surface mismatches and reassign alerts to SRE.
olee: we should also check quota accounting: even though gateway attributes correctly now, ensure billing/usage dashboards don't aggregate cross-org metrics during the window. add a metric scrub for the 12:34–12:50 window.
ojess: thanks. will file a customer incident note if we see any outgoing support tickets.
owen: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/edge-proxy/pull/472 — draft, includes tests for cache key generation.
deploy-bot: deploy job queued: edge-proxy/patch-472 -> canary 5%
opriya: added telemetry card: Console Prefetch Key Mismatch (tile id: dash-834) and alert threshold at 5 mismatches/min
olee: follow-up tasks: (1) automated unit test on cache key includes X-Org-Id when endpoint flagged, (2) add docs for header whitelist rationale, (3) run a one-off scrub on telemetry/billing for the affected window.
ojess: nice. one more ask — let's also add an integration test that simulates rapid org-switching in the UI to catch racey UI prefetch returns.
owen: yes — I'll add a Cypress test and a small e2e in staging. target merge + canary before EOD.
jess: thanks team :thumbsup: keep me posted if you need the repro account creds.
